notes: Moved the visible Quickhack Authority confirmation to the end of the successful ADK loader sequence and delay it briefly so it appears after the normal DEV/Cyberdeck readiness toasts instead of being buried by them.
No Quickhack mechanics changed.
ADK DEV LOADER now shows a visible Foundry toast whenever the Quickhack Authority module loads: FEHA // QUICKHACK AUTHORITY ONLINE // v<version>.
The existing console confirmation remains in place. No Quickhack mechanics changed in this release.
ADK DEV LOADER now prints a clear console confirmation after Cyber Core initialization: FEHA DEV // QUICKHACK AUTHORITY // LOADED // v<version>.
No Quickhack mechanics changed in this release; this is a visibility/debugging-only loader update.

Added FEHA_QUICKHACK_AUTHORITY: a dedicated validated player-to-GM execution bridge for Quickhack mutations. Players keep normal Foundry permissions while the active GM client silently performs allowlisted Quickhack changes.
Quickhack damage no longer creates GM APPLY DAMAGE / DENY chat approval cards. The player's existing damage application now routes through silent GM authority and resolves without a second GM click.
Multiplayer Sync 0.3.0 delegates Quickhack damage to the authority module and no longer installs the Quickhack approval-card click handler or approval-message settlement hook.
The authority module validates the requesting user, owned/assigned operator, loaded Quickhack, target scene/token/actor, and operation before changing any GM-owned document.

The first authority operations are damage plus future-facing sanitized target item listing, Chrome Lock equip-state changes, and Dead Trigger BROKEN renaming. Item operations are hard-restricted to their matching canonical Quickhack.
Dead Trigger's authority operation renames a selected firearm to BROKEN // <original name> and records the original name; it does not apply a status effect.
Player UI wording now says APPLYING DAMAGE rather than AWAITING GM APPROVAL.

Rewrote all 20 Quickhack descriptions into D&D-style ability language: explicit action/reaction timing, target selection, saving-throw phrasing, durations, and resolution order while preserving the 0.10.132 mechanics.
Raised Quickhack market prices substantially while keeping the same Mk balance: Mk.I €$2,500; Mk.II €$6,000; Mk.III €$15,000; Mk.IV €$35,000; Mk.V €$80,000.
The catalog migration marker is now 3.1 so world items and owned copies refresh to the new wording and prices on GM load.
Renamed all 20 Quickhacks into concise in-world software names and rebalanced Mk tier, RAM cost, price, and availability around their rewritten effects.

Mk.I now covers narrow utility (Ghost Key, Wiretap); Mk.II covers tactical utility/control (Dead Air, Chrome Lock, Motor Lock, Network Sweep, Lure); Mk.III covers reliable combat/control tools (Optic Zero, Cookoff, Frenzy, Blank Slate, Dead Trigger).

Mk.IV now contains elite encounter-shaping hacks (Synapse Burn, Toxic Bloom, Rollback, Self-Terminate, System Collapse); Mk.V is reserved for the most extreme effects (Arc Overload, Combustion, Puppet Wire).
RAM was rebalanced with effect strength and reliability: no-save control/AoE and encounter-defining effects cost substantially more, while narrow utility was reduced.
Quickhack migration now updates world items and owned copies with canonical name, Mk/rating/tier, RAM, price, availability, tier identity, effect text, and visible item-description labels.
V3 Quickhack resolution now prefers canonical catalog metadata for save and damage parsing so natural player-facing wording cannot break damage/save resolution.

Reworded the rewritten Quickhack effects to read like natural ability text instead of designer notes. Mechanical metadata such as save bypasses remains internal rather than being printed as phrases like 'No save.'
Quickhack mechanics and RAM costs from 0.10.130 are unchanged; this pass only cleans the player-facing wording and bumps the rewrite marker so existing world and owned copies are refreshed.
Rewrote the full 20-item Quickhack catalog into a single canonical FEHA_QUICKHACK_CATALOG module so RAM/effect definitions are no longer scattered across stale item descriptions.

Blind is now full Blinded for 1 turn unless the target has blindsense; Brain Melt is 10d6 psychic; Breach Protocol opens a locked networked door; Comms Call In taps a failed-Wisdom target's comms; Comms Noise Deafens for 2 turns and blocks comms.

Contagion is now an instantaneous placeable 10-ft gas burst for 8d6 poison; EMP Overload is 12d12 lightning with failed-save reaction loss; Grenade Explode has no save and uses the explosive's own damage/radius; Locomotion Malfunction is legs-only with no save.

Overheat Program is renamed Combustion Program: 10d6 immediate fire, with a 5d6 fire death-burst in 10 ft. Ping reveals network devices plus cyberware-equipped hostiles. Suicide and System Collapse no longer have per-target combat limits.

Generic Program is now a reaction-style forced lower reroll plus advantage rider; Memory Wipe erases the previous minute after an operator-chosen save; Take Control uses a Charisma save for up to 1 minute with vision sharing and ends after a hostile/damaging action.

System Collapse RAM is now 6; Take Control RAM is 6; Weapon Malfunction RAM is 5 and permanently breaks one wielded firearm until repaired. Other Quickhack RAM values remain at their current balanced values unless explicitly changed.
GM load now migrates both world-catalog and already-owned actor Quickhack copies to the canonical names/effectText/RAM values while preserving surrounding item-sheet/market markup.
Player Quickhack damage now uses a GM chat approval card instead of automatic socket authority: player clicks APPLY DAMAGE, GM clicks APPLY DAMAGE in chat, and the HP update happens on the GM client.
Approval cards are whispered to GM users plus the requester and include APPLY DAMAGE / DENY; resolved cards replace themselves with the final HP change and approving GM name.
The player Quickhack panel shows AWAITING GM APPROVAL while pending. Denial, approval errors, or the 10-minute expiry feed the existing failure path so committed RAM is refunded.
Quickhack completion is settled from the synchronized ChatMessage update, removing the fragile GM socket-response dependency for damage.
GM-originated Quickhack damage still applies immediately without an approval card.

The existing Foundry hotbar Macro named ADK DEV LOADER / ADK DEV LOADER V3 is now intercepted client-side and redirected to the player-safe local reload function before any stale historical GM-only macro body can run.
Players no longer need the GM to edit or re-save the old world Macro just to use the reloader; other macros still execute normally.
This changes only the reloader entry point. It does not grant player clients GM permissions for world-document mutations.

Fixed Quickhack authority timeout when the player client is freshly reloaded but the GM client is still running an older FEHA authority handler: requests now include a concrete known GM user id even when the player's active-GM presence cache is stale.
This preserves compatibility with older handlers that reject gmId:null, avoiding silent socket drops after a player-only ADK reload.
Authority timeouts now explicitly report that no GM client answered the socket request.
Quickhack damage now attempts the target Actor update locally first, so a player who already has sufficient Foundry ownership no longer requires any GM/DM client or authority route.
If Foundry actually rejects the local HP write for permissions, the Quickhack falls back to silent GM authority routing; there is still no approval dialog.
Player clients no longer hard-fail solely because game.users.activeGM is empty/stale: Quickhack authority requests can broadcast to the module socket and be claimed by a live GM client.
A truly unowned NPC with no live GM remains subject to Foundry's server permission model; the client does not fabricate or bypass server permissions.

ADK reloading is now explicitly client-local and player-safe: every connected user gets game.adk.reload(), game.adk.reloadDev(), game.adk.reloadCurrentClient(), and FEHA_ADK_RELOAD with no GM/DM authority check.
A reload refreshes only the invoking browser client's FEHA runtime; it does not request GM approval and does not grant the player GM world-write permissions.
FEHA_CLIENT_BOOTSTRAP now installs the local reload API and reuses the same validated repo loader path for both initial boot and manual client reloads.
Player Quickhack HP mutation now always routes through GM authority instead of trusting targetActor.isOwner, avoiding synthetic/unlinked token ownership false-positives.
GM authority now resolves the Quickhack target exclusively from the authoritative Scene Token instead of comparing a client-supplied Actor id, fixing synthetic/unlinked token id mismatches.
The authority validator accepts the user's assigned character as the operator even when legacy Actor ownership metadata is not normalized to OWNER.
Quickhack failure toasts now include the actual authority/update error message so any remaining multiplayer failure is directly diagnosable.
No manual GM approval was added; successful Quickhacks remain one-click from the player client.

Fixed Quickhack resolution incorrectly freezing APPLY DAMAGE as AUTHORITY OFFLINE from a stale/preflight GM-presence check; the button now remains actionable whenever the resolved target Actor exists and authority is resolved at click time.
Switched multiplayer, Network Device, and Camera authority selection to Foundry v14 game.users.activeGM first, with the prior deterministic active-GM scan retained as fallback.
Player Quickhack damage against an unowned target still routes silently through GM authority; there is no manual GM approval dialog.
No Entry Gateway or JACK IN cinematic timing changed.
Added FEHA Multiplayer Sync on every connected client: Market vendor/tier state, stock changes, actor/item surfaces, and device Scene updates now reconcile live across GM and player clients.
Market purchases are reconciled by deterministic GM authority against shared world stock; stale simultaneous duplicate purchases are removed and refunded instead of duplicating limited stock.
Player Quickhack damage against unowned targets now routes automatically through the active GM authority with no manual GM permission/approval step; RAM commit/refund behavior remains unchanged.
Network Probe creation now uses silent GM authority instead of the manual approval queue; Network Device commands and reveals remain authority-validated and automatic.

Market, Chrome, Cyberdeck, and Wallet opening now route player clients to their assigned/owned character while preserving GM control; GM helper APIs can also open a specific UI on a specific online player's client.
No Entry Gateway or JACK IN cinematic timing values were changed.
Added FEHA Live Dev Bridge: a Foundry module bootstrap that runs on every connected client and loads the same validated GitHub dev runtime for players and GM on world join.
ADK_DEV_LOADER is now client-safe instead of GM-only; player clients use the same immutable-commit preflight/swap path while world mutations remain protected by the existing GM-authority modules.
Player join temporarily hides the legacy Entry Gateway while the current build attaches, with a timed fallback that restores the installed gateway if the live bridge cannot load.

Entry Gateway normalization now watches for late legacy gateway roots from duplicate/older gateway modules and removes them immediately, preventing the old gateway from rendering underneath or on top of the new one.
Gateway replacement now removes every duplicate #adk-entry-gateway root rather than only the first matching element.
Gateway cancellation now settles tracked sleep Promises and stops each cinematic/boot/auth async flow cleanly instead of leaving unresolved closures after close, reopen, bypass, or hot reload.
Gateway delayed terminal scrolling and the final glitch/split launch timer now share the tracked timeout registry and are cancelled consistently.
Entry Gateway teardown restores only API methods/candidate data still owned by FEHA, so later module overrides are not overwritten.
Credits Wallet teardown now preserves pre-existing getCredits/setCredits/addCredits/spendCredits methods and restores only API slots still occupied by FEHA's own replacements.
A final reduced-motion rule now covers the later 0.10.117 real glitch strips as well as pseudo-letter ghosts; normal visuals are unchanged.
Deep-pass follow-up: Network Device specialized adapters now execute only on the GM-authoritative path; player callers cannot self-promote remote/skip-breach context.
Quickhack damage now commits RAM before mutating target HP, closing the free-damage race when RAM changes after preview; if HP mutation fails, a guarded RAM refund is attempted.
Quickhack RAM commits/refunds hold an action lock while actor flags update, preventing the visible Cyberdeck from rerendering mid-transaction.
Chat-message failures are now non-fatal after a Quickhack gameplay mutation succeeds, so a failed chat log can no longer re-enable an already-applied action.
Non-damage Quickhacks that are resisted now show COMMIT ATTEMPT / RESISTED // RAM SPENT instead of falsely claiming EFFECT APPLIED.
Legacy actor identity normalization now maps Raiden to Zach and Sasha Bogdanov to Sasha consistently in Chrome subject theming and the V3 roster.
GM-created Network Probes now settle locally even if the socket transport does not echo to the sender; probe approval timeout increased to ten minutes.

Deep stability audit: ADK DEV LOADER now fetches and preflights all JS/CSS plus version.json before destroying the currently working runtime, so network failures, syntax failures, and partial multi-file commits no longer take down a good build.
Loader now rejects V3/version.json mismatches before swap and verifies the loaded V3 version after evaluation; failed post-swap loads attempt a clean V2 fallback.
Cyber Core now propagates module initialization failures instead of logging them and falsely reporting a successful load.
Network approvals now choose one deterministic active GM for probe, device-command, and reveal requests, preventing duplicate execution in multi-GM sessions.
Network approval RPCs now time out/cancel cleanly on reload; Network Probes have a two-minute approval timeout instead of an unbounded pending Promise.
Camera authority RPCs now cancel timers and settle pending requests cleanly on module reload; socket init is idempotent.
